101: A is correct because a NAT gateway is the AWS-managed, highly available way to allow instances in private subnets to initiate outbound internet connections, such as downloading software updates, while blocking unsolicited inbound connections. Deploying one NAT gateway in the public subnet of each AZ, with a per-AZ private route table sending 0.0.0.0/0 to the NAT gateway in its own AZ, avoids cross-AZ traffic charges and removes any single point of failure. Self-managed NAT instances lack automatic failover, a VPC can only have one internet gateway, and an egress-only internet gateway is an IPv6 feature.
102: B and E are correct because AWS DataSync is the managed service purpose-built to automate and accelerate transfers of on-premises NFS data into AWS, and it can write directly to an Amazon EFS file system. B is correct because a DataSync agent must be deployed in the on-premises data center to connect to and read from the SFTP server's NFS file system holding the 200 GB of data. E is correct because you must configure a suitable DataSync location for the on-premises NFS storage (with the EFS file system as the destination) so the transfer task knows its source and target. This fully automates the migration without manual copy commands or extra EBS volumes.
103: A is correct because AWS Glue job bookmarks store state that tracks which input records have already been processed, so each daily run processes only the newly added XML data in the S3 bucket. This prevents reprocessing old data and reduces both job runtime and cost. It is the built-in, purpose-designed feature for incremental processing, unlike approaches that delete data or reduce worker counts.
104: A and C are correct because together they provide purpose-built DDoS mitigation plus edge absorption of the attack traffic. A is correct because AWS Shield Advanced provides 24/7 DDoS response support and sophisticated mitigations for large-scale volumetric attacks from thousands of IP addresses, which is required when downtime is unacceptable. C is correct because Amazon CloudFront sits at the edge and absorbs and filters attack traffic before it reaches the origin EC2 instances, protecting both static and dynamic content and shielding the Windows web servers from the flood.
105: D is correct because a resource-based policy attached to the Lambda function is the mechanism for granting another AWS service permission to invoke it, and scoping it to only lambda:InvokeFunction with the Service principal events.amazonaws.com follows least privilege. EventBridge gets exactly the single action it needs and nothing more. An execution role defines what the function's own code may access when it runs, not which service may invoke the function, so it is the wrong instrument here.
106: D is correct because SSE-KMS encrypts the objects with an AWS KMS key, and every use of that key is automatically recorded in AWS CloudTrail, satisfying the audit-logging requirement. Automatic rotation means KMS rotates the underlying key material once per year with no data re-encryption or administrative action, which is the most operationally efficient approach. Manual rotation adds recurring overhead, and SSE-S3 and SSE-C do not provide KMS-level key usage logs.
107: B is correct because Amazon API Gateway provides the managed REST API front end while AWS Lambda provides the serverless compute to receive, process, and store the bicycle location data points, making them accessible through the REST API for the analytics platform. This pairing scales automatically with peak-hour volumes and requires no servers to manage. The other options are analytics or stream-processing tools that do not themselves expose a REST interface for storing and retrieving data.
108: A is correct because an AWS Lambda function triggered when the database on Amazon RDS is updated can push the sold automobile's data to an Amazon SQS queue, which decouples the website from the multiple target systems. Each target then consumes the message from the queue independently, providing reliable, loosely coupled delivery to every consumer. A standard queue is sufficient because strict ordering is not a stated requirement, so FIFO adds unnecessary complexity.
109: D is correct because S3 Object Lock with versioning enforced on the bucket makes objects immutable, and a legal hold provides protection for an indefinite, nonspecific period, exactly matching the requirement that objects remain unchangeable until the company decides otherwise. Granting s3:PutObjectLegalHold only to specific users' IAM policies ensures only those users can lift the hold to modify or delete the objects. A fixed retention mode such as 100 years in governance mode is not indefinite and is less flexible.
110: C and D are correct because they remove the synchronous image processing from the EC2 web servers, which is the cause of the slow uploads and tight coupling. C is correct because a presigned URL allows each user's browser to upload the original image directly to Amazon S3, so upload traffic never touches the web tier. D is correct because S3 Event Notifications can trigger a Lambda function to resize each uploaded image asynchronously and store the result in S3. This decoupled design improves website performance with minimal operational effort.
111: D is correct because Amazon MQ with active/standby brokers across two Availability Zones provides a managed, automatically failed-over replacement for the self-managed ActiveMQ queue. An Auto Scaling group of consumer EC2 instances across two AZs keeps message processing running through instance or AZ failures. Amazon RDS for MySQL with Multi-AZ enabled gives the MySQL layer automatic synchronous standby failover without manual replication, yielding the highest availability with low operational complexity compared to self-managed components.
112: A is correct because AWS Fargate with Amazon ECS runs the existing containerized application unchanged, so code changes and development effort are minimal, and Fargate removes all server management. Service Auto Scaling adjusts the number of tasks to match the growing request volume, and an Application Load Balancer distributes the incoming requests across them. This serverless container approach has less operational overhead than managing EC2 instances, rewriting the app for Lambda, or standing up an HPC cluster.
113: C is correct because the data center has no available network bandwidth, so ordering an AWS Snowball Edge Storage Optimized device is the fastest and most practical way to move 50 TB of data to AWS. Once the data is imported, AWS Glue provides a fully managed environment to run the weekly custom transformation job in the cloud with the least operational overhead. DataSync depends on network bandwidth that is not available, and running the app on a small Snowcone or a new EC2 instance adds unnecessary effort.
114: C is correct because AWS Lambda scales automatically and independently to match the significantly varying number of concurrent users, and Amazon S3 provides durable, highly scalable, low-cost object storage for the photo files. Retaining DynamoDB for metadata keeps the existing data model with single-digit millisecond performance at any scale. This serverless design absorbs spiky traffic without over-provisioning fixed infrastructure like additional EC2 instances with io2 EBS volumes.
115: C is correct because a gateway VPC endpoint for Amazon S3 provides a private path from inside the VPC to S3 over the AWS network, so file transfer traffic never traverses the internet. Moving the EC2 instances to private subnets and linking the endpoint to the private route tables removes their internet exposure entirely since S3 is the only access they need. A NAT gateway still sends traffic over the internet, security groups alone do not change the traffic path, and Direct Connect is a costly heavyweight change when a free gateway endpoint suffices.
116: A and D are correct because they replace the patching-heavy CMS with a fully managed, serverless static architecture. D is correct because hosting the new website as a static site on Amazon S3 eliminates all server patching and maintenance and scales automatically to serve the content. A is correct because Amazon CloudFront in front of the S3 site provides edge caching for high scalability and HTTPS termination for enhanced security. With no dynamic content and only four updates a year, no compute fleet is needed.
117: A is correct because CloudWatch Logs has a built-in subscription feature that streams log data directly to Amazon OpenSearch Service in near real time, entirely within managed services and with no custom code or infrastructure. This native integration is the least operationally overhead path. The alternatives require building or operating extra components such as Lambda functions, delivery streams, or agents on every application server.
118: D is correct because Amazon S3 is the most cost-effective storage for 900 TB of static text documents, scales automatically with no capacity planning to meet periods of high demand, and serves the documents durably to EC2 instances across multiple Availability Zones. Block and file storage would cost dramatically more at this scale, and OpenSearch Service is a search analytics service rather than general document storage.
119: B is correct because AWS Firewall Manager is designed to centrally configure and manage AWS WAF rules across multiple AWS accounts and multiple Regions from one place, which minimizes administrative effort for protecting the API Gateway stages against SQL injection and cross-site scripting. Deploying WAF separately in each Region and account would require duplicated manual configuration. Shield addresses DDoS attacks, not injection or XSS attacks.
120: B is correct because AWS Global Accelerator uses static anycast IP addresses at the AWS edge network to route user traffic to the closest healthy endpoint group, and endpoint groups in us-west-2 and eu-west-1 with the two NLBs as endpoints provide automatic health-check-based failover. This improves performance and availability for users in the United States and Europe while supporting the DNS traffic, which includes non-HTTP protocols that CloudFront cannot proxy, and avoids the manual regional steering of Route 53 geolocation records.
